scope: Leptos book and API documentation; official router/server crates named separately.

ssr.note: The ssr build mode generates server HTML; hydrate builds activate it in the browser.

streaming.note: In-order, out-of-order, and partially blocked SSR modes are documented.

suspense.note: Suspense boundaries coordinate resources and stream resolved content with fallback UI in out-of-order mode.

client.note: The hydrate feature adds interactivity to server-rendered HTML; islands is a separate opt-in mode.
client.label: Hydration / islands

ssg.note: StaticRouteGenerator and static route lists generate HTML files; dynamic parameters must be enumerated.
ssg.label: leptos_axum

csr.note: The csr feature renders the application in the browser; hydrate and ssr are separate build modes.

serverOnly.note: Islands keep non-interactive component work on the server; server functions also exclude their bodies from browser builds. This is not RSC.
serverOnly.label: Islands / server functions

partialRendering.note: SSR modes control per-request streaming; the guide does not establish a prebuilt static shell with request-time dynamic holes.

routing.note: leptos_router provides nested Routes and route parameters.
routing.label: leptos_router

layouts.note: Nested routes and Outlet compose layouts around child pages.
layouts.label: leptos_router

dynamicRoutes.note: Route parameters and query values can be read and parsed into typed values.
dynamicRoutes.label: leptos_router

parallelRoutes.note: Nested Outlet routes are documented; independent named route slots are not established.

interceptedRoutes.note: The reviewed router guide does not establish intercepted-modal/direct-entry route behavior.

prefetch.note: The reviewed A component API resolves nested links and active state; automatic route/data prefetch is not established.

softNavigation.note: leptos_router enhances local links, changes routes/history and updates the route outlet in the browser without a document reload.
softNavigation.label: leptos_router

viewTransitions.note: Routes/FlatRoutes expose a transition flag to coordinate the browser View Transition API during navigation. Browser support and application CSS determine the animation; asynchronous UI Transition is a separate concept.
viewTransitions.label: leptos_router transition

redirects.note: Server integrations expose redirects and response options; router redirects handle client navigation.
redirects.label: Router / server integrations

serverData.note: Resource resolves asynchronous work on the server and serializes its value for hydration.

clientData.note: Resource and LocalResource react to dependencies and expose asynchronous client data. Shared query caching needs additional policy.

requestDedupe.note: Resource sharing is possible through context, but an automatic request-wide keyed deduplication cache is not established.

persistentCache.note: Static routes retain generated page files. This is a page-generation mechanism, not a general-purpose application data cache.
persistentCache.label: Static routes

invalidation.note: Actions expose reactive versions/results that can drive Resource refetching. This is distinct from a path/tag server cache.
invalidation.label: Reactive resource refetch

isr.note: Static route regeneration functions define when generated pages should be refreshed. Applications supply the trigger and host/storage configuration.
isr.label: RegenerationFn

apiRoutes.note: Axum/Actix integrations expose generated server-function routes and can be composed with custom HTTP handlers.
apiRoutes.label: leptos_axum / leptos_actix

httpErrors.note: The Axum/Actix integrations expose ResponseOptions to set status and headers during SSR or a server function. A view showing “not found” must explicitly choose 404; a visual ErrorBoundary alone does not do so. With streaming, make the decision before headers are sent; later failures cannot replace the committed HTTP status.
httpErrors.label: ResponseOptions / integrations

actions.note: The #[server] macro generates server endpoints and browser call stubs.
actions.label: server_fn

forms.note: ActionForm progressively enhances ServerAction forms and works without client JS. Applications still validate server-side inputs.
forms.label: leptos_router ActionForm

assessment.summary: Form transport, validation, pending feedback and optimistic state are separate behaviors; the progressive-forms and optimistic-updates rows review the latter contracts explicitly.
strengths: ActionForm progressively enhances ServerAction forms and works without client JS. Applications still validate server-side inputs.
tradeoffs: Do not infer a no-JavaScript submission path, automatic validation, accessible field errors or rollback merely from the ability to receive FormData.

middleware.note: Server functions integrate host extractors and Axum/Actix request middleware.
middleware.label: Server integrations

cookies.note: ResponseOptions and host extractors can read/set cookie headers; session storage/policy is application-owned.
cookies.label: Server integrations

cssModules.note: Stylance maps CSS/SCSS modules into Rust class references.
cssModules.label: Stylance

scopedCss.note: Stylers supplies scoped inline CSS; Stylance offers external stylesheet modules.
scopedCss.label: Stylers / Stylance

tailwind.note: cargo-leptos can run Tailwind’s external compiler as part of its build workflow.
tailwind.label: cargo-leptos recipe

cssInJs.note: Rust scoped-style packages are documented; a JavaScript CSS-in-JS SSR registry is not established.

images.note: Styles/asset builds are documented; an automatic image resizing/format pipeline is not established.

fonts.note: Fonts may be authored in CSS; a font download/subset/fallback-optimization API is not established.

scripts.note: leptos_meta manages script elements in the head; sophisticated third-party scheduling is application-owned.
scripts.label: leptos_meta Script

assetPipeline.note: cargo-leptos can add hashes to generated CSS, JS, and WASM filenames with hash-files enabled; it is off by default and the server must use matching configuration. Files from assets-dir are copied, so arbitrary images such as image.svg still need application-owned versioning.
assetPipeline.label: JS, CSS & WASM hashing

staticAssets.note: cargo-leptos builds client assets and copies configured public assets into the site output.
staticAssets.label: cargo-leptos

metadata.note: leptos_meta supplies Title, Meta, Link, and other head components. It is component-based rather than a merged metadata object.
metadata.label: Reactive head components

assessment.label: Reactive head components
assessment.summary: Head elements participate in the reactive component model, with a documented title formatter.
strengths: Title, Meta, Link, and other head components can be authored within application components.
Reactive values update metadata; a shared formatter composes route titles.
tradeoffs: This review has not established a general nested metadata-object merge/clear contract.
Do not infer Next.js-equivalent inheritance behavior from the presence of a Meta component.

dynamicMetadata.note: Metadata components accept reactive values, so document metadata can follow application state.
dynamicMetadata.label: leptos_meta

metadataInheritance.note: Reactive head components and context compose metadata; the Title formatter can be inherited independently of child title text. General nested metadata-object merging is not established.
metadataInheritance.label: Title/context composition

metadataOverrides.note: Child Title text can compose with an ancestor formatter. A uniform nested SEO-field merge/clear contract is not established.
metadataOverrides.label: Title-specific composition

titleTemplates.note: Title accepts a formatter on the app and route-specific text. The book demonstrates a common suffix applied to route titles.
titleTemplates.label: Title formatter

socialImages.note: Head meta/link components do not establish a generated social-card image renderer.

sitemaps.note: Route definitions do not themselves establish automatic crawler XML sitemap generation.

robots.note: An application can publish an authored robots.txt from its configured assets directory.
robots.label: Public file

markdown.note: The reviewed view/component and build APIs do not establish a Markdown content pipeline; an additional parser/build step is needed.

collections.note: The build guide does not establish typed content collection schemas/loaders/query registries.

draftMode.note: Application response/cache logic is available; a dedicated authenticated draft-preview API is not established.

translations.note: leptos_i18n supplies locale-aware translated messages for Leptos applications.
translations.label: leptos_i18n

localeRouting.note: The reviewed leptos_i18n API establishes locale context/messages, but a locale-aware URL router/negotiation contract is not established here.

localeFormatting.note: leptos_i18n’s formatters include ICU-backed number/date/time formatting; enable the relevant package features.
localeFormatting.label: leptos_i18n

auth.note: Host extractors can supply an authenticated user to server functions. Login, identity storage, and authorization remain application/library work.
auth.label: Host auth extractors

csp.note: The nonce feature generates request nonces and applies them to framework inline scripts/styles. Configure the matching CSP policy in the host response.
csp.label: Nonce feature

cspNonce.note: The nonce feature generates request nonces and applies them to framework inline scripts/styles. Configure the matching CSP policy in the host response.
cspNonce.label: Nonce feature

csrf.note: Server functions are public endpoints; the reviewed macro guide does not establish a complete CSRF token/origin protection policy. Applications must secure endpoints.

environment.note: Server-function implementations are excluded from client builds; applications must keep secrets out of serialized return values.
environment.label: Server-function boundary

types.note: Rust types and view macros check typed component composition during compilation.

hmr.note: cargo-leptos watch rebuilds and reloads the app; CSS/assets can update without a full source rebuild.
hmr.label: cargo-leptos

cli.note: cargo-leptos integrates build, watch, test, and asset processing.
cli.label: cargo-leptos

bundleAnalysis.note: The reviewed CLI build workflow does not establish a graphical production bundle/module analyzer.

unitTests.note: The guide demonstrates native Rust tests and wasm-bindgen-test for browser-side code.
unitTests.label: Rust / wasm-bindgen-test

e2eTests.note: The testing guide uses Playwright against the running application.
e2eTests.label: Playwright

observability.note: leptos::logging supplies log/warn/error macros for the browser console or native terminal. The debug_* variants are debug-build-only. Structured tracing, collection/export and production monitoring remain host/integration work.
observability.label: Isomorphic logging macros

errorHandling.note: ErrorBoundary renders fallback UI for errors carried by child views.

serverHosting.note: Axum/Actix applications can run as production binaries on VMs.
serverHosting.label: Server integrations

subpathProxy.note: The non-root deployment guide coordinates Router base, HydrationScripts root and the server-function URL. It explicitly describes a proxy stripping the prefix and using different server/browser router bases. Asset hosting and public-origin/forwarded-header policy remain part of the Axum/Actix deployment.
subpathProxy.label: Router / server integration

staticHosting.note: CSR builds can be served as static files; request-time SSR/server functions still need a server.
staticHosting.label: CSR static deployment

containers.note: The official guide includes Docker/Podman multi-stage build recipes.
containers.label: Container recipe

edgeHosting.note: Leptos-Axum documents JS-hosted WASM targets including Cloudflare/Deno; dependencies must be WASM-compatible and setup differs.
edgeHosting.label: WASM server integration

orm.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned orm / query builder API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

migrations.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned schema migrations API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

transactions.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned transactions API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

jobs.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned background jobs API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

mail.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned email API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

uploads.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned file uploads & storage API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

realtime.note: The reviewed framework documentation does not establish an owned real-time delivery API. Host libraries and application integrations may provide it.

xssEscaping.note: view! renders dynamic strings as text; inner_html inserts raw HTML and requires trusted/sanitized input. Rendering text safely does not make untrusted HTML safe.

htmlSanitization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific html sanitization contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

authorization.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific authorization policies contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

rateLimiting.note: The linked security API review does not establish the specific rate limiting contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

progressiveEnhancement.note: ActionForm maps server functions to a native form submission and enhances it when hydrated. Input types/encoding must support form submission; browser-only events do not supply a no-JS fallback.
progressiveEnhancement.label: leptos_router ActionForm

optimisticUi.note: Actions expose input/pending/value and the book demonstrates deriving optimistic state from pending submissions. Application code still chooses merge/error behavior; a pending flag alone is not an optimistic update.
optimisticUi.label: Actions / pending input

requestCancellation.note: The linked data API review does not establish the specific stale request handling contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

typedLinks.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific typed links & parameters contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchParams.note: Params-derived query structs parse search values into typed Results; applications handle malformed values and defaults. Reading a raw ParamsMap is a separate, less constrained API.
searchParams.label: leptos_router Params

stateRestoration.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific navigation state retention contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scrollRestoration.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific scroll restoration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

navigationBlocking.note: The linked routing API review does not establish the specific unsaved-change guards contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

navigationAccessibility.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessible navigation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

a11yChecks.note: The linked client rendering API review does not establish the specific accessibility checks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

lazyActivation.note: The linked rendering API review does not establish the specific deferred activation contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

codeSplitting.note: The official lazy_routes example uses LazyRoute and cargo leptos watch --split to load route-specific browser WASM/code. It requires the opt-in split toolchain and is distinct from enabling islands; shared code and toolchain support constrain the resulting chunks.
codeSplitting.label: Router / cargo-leptos

offline.note: The linked deployment API review does not establish the specific offline integration contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

scheduling.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific scheduled tasks contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

notifications.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific multi-channel notifications contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

searchIndex.note: The linked backend API review does not establish the specific search indexing contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

fieldEncryption.note: The linked database API review does not establish the specific encrypted model fields contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.

httpTests.note: The linked testing API review does not establish the specific http integration tests contract defined here. This is a bounded documentation finding, not proof of absence; generic hooks or application-authored code are not counted as an owned implementation.
